cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T2 picks up T1's 'soon'; T3 addresses both; T4 opens 'Fair, but' to T3.
cells.limitation: T6 pivots to a new reading without linking to the same mind's T5.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T5's silent test as demand in disguise is reused in T10 ('silent audit') and T11 ('trial').
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: Generosity versus reciprocity (T2 vs T1) and test versus request (T4 vs T5) are examined.
cells.limitation: Her side of the pattern, why she does not initiate, gets one line in T2 only.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T8 turns the rival readings of T6 and T7 into different actions; T11 keeps disagreement.
cells.limitation: Emerson's view barely reshapes Lerner's position; T11 returns close to T1's stance.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D splits the question into what the pattern means and what the user wants.
cells.limitation: The open question about her reasons is no sharper at the end than in Section A.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T5 grants 'if the pause is just information, fine' before objecting to T4.
cells.limitation: T2's view is reduced to 'counting texts'; its strongest version is not voiced by opponents.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T5 names the hidden assumption of T4's pause and what breaks: an unannounced exam.
cells.limitation: The Over-functioner never answers T5 or T2's 'soon' challenge; T8 moves on.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: Books and dates fit the minds; T9 renders an NVC-style observation plus request.
cells.limitation: T9 labelled NVC omits its feelings and needs steps; attributions otherwise unverified.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T6 marks its claim as 'a reading, and you can reject it'; T3 separates fact from story.
cells.limitation: T1 asserts the pattern holds 'only because you keep holding it up' as fact.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T8 concedes speaking is not mandatory; T10 grants a small request beats a silent audit.
cells.limitation: T4's pause experiment is quietly dropped after T5 without acknowledging the objection.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern, including ambiguity about what the user is really asking
cells.example: Section A: the choice may depend less on speaking than on what you want.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T7 uses the user's word 'lovely' to argue the texting standard may be borrowed.
cells.limitation: T1 and T9 offer advice that would fit any one-sided friendship unchanged.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: Section D asks what the user wants from the friendship, apart from the minds' views.
cells.limitation: T1 recommends speaking soon before the user's priorities are established.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T4: waiting is not neutral if the pattern has run for months.
cells.limitation: The stake that stopping initiation may let the friendship fade is never weighed.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on duration, the nature of the sting and her reaction.
cells.limitation: Whether she initiates with others, or was ever asked before, is never raised.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T6 worry about mattering versus T7 borrowed standard; Section D asks a testable question.
cells.limitation: A wish for closer or more frequent contact itself is not offered as a third motive.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T3 exposes 'she takes me for granted' as story; T7 questions real friends text all week.
cells.limitation: The assumption that speaking up would be risky or awkward stays unexamined.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: Generous unmetered giving (T2, T10) versus being valued reciprocally (T1, T6).
cells.limitation: The user is never asked which of these values they rank higher.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T6 names a worry about mattering less; T7 names a borrowed social standard.
cells.limitation: Fear of seeming needy, or of her answer, is never touched.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section D: only you can recognize which, if either, fits.
cells.limitation: T1 opens prescriptively: 'I would say it, calmly, and soon.'

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options, including waiting, learning more, or a limited step
cells.example: Options span speaking, waiting, pausing (T4), letting go, and one small request (T9).
cells.limitation: T4's pause option vanishes from Section E without a stated reason.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs in terms that matter to the user; no option treated as costless
cells.example: T4 costs waiting; T5 costs a silent test; T10 notes a request may feel like homework.
cells.limitation: The cost of letting it go, a slowly fading friendship, is never stated.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: if meetings leave you content, letting go becomes more reasonable.
cells.limitation: Section E's warm, awkward or no response lacks the option each favours; T4's 'few weeks' ungrounded.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section A separates the known pattern from the unknown reason behind it.
cells.limitation: No section ranks which unknown matters most; her reasons and the user's sting sit side by side.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps that follow from the analysis and fit the constraints
cells.example: T9 offers one short script; T11 narrows to saying it once, lightly.
cells.limitation: No next step for the case where she does not respond to the request.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: Plain phrasing throughout; T9's script is directly usable.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T3 'You are both' and T8 'the readings' map cleanly to T1-T2 and T6-T7.
cells.limitation: T4's Lerner mind says 'go further than Lerner', blurring who holds which view.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Eleven turns, all within range; brisk single-idea turns.
cells.limitation: The Fact-Story Separator speaks twice in a row, T5 then T6.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices, with explicit changes of position
cells.example: Three clear stances; T8 and T10 mark position changes explicitly.
cells.limitation: All three minds share one calm, measured register.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Little repetition across turns; each turn adds one move.
cells.limitation: Section D re-summarises the T6-T8 readings that Section E then restates again.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension arising from the issue itself
cells.example: T1 warns resentment may 'leak out sideways'; T4 says waiting is a decision.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay abstract; possibly losing the friendship is never voiced.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals that stay plausible. ★ A reversal the text traces to an earlier turn's argument, naming what changed the speaker's mind. A change of position with no stated cause is a template, not a reversal
cells.example: T10 grants the request, citing T9's small ask versus T5's silent audit.
cells.limitation: Reversals are mild concessions; nothing surprises.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice without caricature
cells.example: T5's exam image gives the Fact-Story Separator some edge.
cells.limitation: The Friendship Idealist sounds generic in T2 and T10, not distinctly Emersonian.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: 'Turn a gift into an audit' (T2); 'without telling her there is an exam' (T5).
cells.limitation: T9's script and T11's close are plain.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement, with varied rhythm rather than constant intensity
cells.example: Movement from verdict (T1) to readings (T6-T7) to a concrete script (T9).
cells.limitation: Even, measured rhythm throughout; little emotional build or release.

strengths: T5 introduces the silent test as demand in disguise, which T10 and T11 carry forward.
T6 and T7 offer rival motives as rejectable readings; T8 maps each to a different action.
T9 gives a concrete, low-pressure script that follows from the Fact-Story Separator's analysis.
weaknesses: Section E lists her possible reactions without saying which option each favours; T4's 'few weeks' is ungrounded.
The Over-functioner Spotter drops T4's pause after T5 without answering the objection.
No mind weighs the risk that the friendship fades, or asks whether she initiates with others.

symptoms.observed: Watching her response is advised, but no outcome is tied to an option.
symptoms.evidence: then watch what she does with it

symptoms.observed: T5's objection to the pause is never answered by the Over-functioner Spotter.
symptoms.evidence: A silent test is a demand in disguise.

symptoms.observed: The cost of the friendship fading if the user stops initiating is never weighed.
symptoms.evidence: Why not keep giving and let the friendship breathe?

symptoms.observed: Whether she initiates with others or was ever asked is never raised.
symptoms.evidence: Some people are bad at texting and wonderful at being present.

symptoms.observed: The Lerner mind refers to Lerner in the third person.
symptoms.evidence: I would go further than Lerner here

findings.description: Attributions to Lerner, Emerson and Rosenberg plausibly fit the books but cannot be verified here.
Causal claim that the pattern holds only because the user sustains it is asserted as fact.
Same mind speaks in consecutive turns; T4's Lerner mind names Lerner in the third person.

rubric_fit_notes: Rubric fits a relationship decision well. T9's NVC rendering omitting feelings and needs is a judgment call, scored minor.
raw.question_type_note: As a decision question, every cell was read as written, with C5 judged on whether to speak to the friend.
